chunks: And from him (Al-Hadith) from Safwan from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who dies without having performed the Hajj of Islam, and leaves behind wealth. He said: 'It is incumbent upon his estate to send a man to perform Hajj on his behalf, who is a stranger (has no wealth of his own).'

key_terms.حَجَّةَ الْإِسْلَامِ: The first obligatory Hajj performed by a Muslim
key_terms.صَرُورَةً: A stranger or one who is not wealthy, often implying a professional pilgrim
key_terms.يَحُجَّ عَنْهُ: To perform Hajj on behalf of another

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a Muslim who dies without performing the obligatory Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the mechanism of *Hajj al-Tamattu'* or *Hajj al-Bada'il* for the deceased, specifying that the proxy must be a *Sarrurah*—a dedicated, non-wealthy individual who performs Hajj for remuneration. This highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on utilizing the deceased's estate to fulfill unperformed religious obligations, ensuring the spiritual debt is settled through a qualified representative rather than a general charity.
